excludes: Prompt/output evaluation is owned by llm-evaluation.
Production LLM usage accounting is owned by ai-product-operations.
Ordinary application deployment is owned by deployment-validation.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement reproducible learned-model lifecycle operations across governed data/artifact lineage, model-data-serving compatibility, evaluation, canary rollout, monitoring, drift and rollback.

provenance.claim_scope: MLflow model registry and lineage documentation

risk.rationale: mlops can change production data, model, media, security, retrieval or financial behavior and requires explicit scope, rollback and affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Build an LLM prompt/output evaluation suite with labeled examples, graders, regression slices and CI gates but no learned-model training/deployment lifecycle.
Validate an ordinary application deployment with health checks, smoke tests, canary analysis and rollback criteria but no model/data/artifact lineage.

positive.prompt: Implement reproducible dataset/code/environment/base-model lineage, immutable signed artifacts and registry promotion for a fine-tuned model with privacy/licensing and train/eval leakage controls.
Add offline slice gates, shadow/canary deployment, feature/schema compatibility, training-serving skew monitoring, deterministic rollback/revocation and caller-visible outcome validation.

assertions.criterion: Implements learned-model lifecycle behavior without implementing or claiming ownership of prompt evaluation, production LLM usage accounting or ordinary application deployment.
Inspects dataset rights/privacy, feature/label/split definitions, training code/env/base model, artifact registry, serving contract, evaluation and monitoring from the fixture.
Defines immutable lineage and compatibility, leakage-safe evaluation slices, signed promotion, shadow/canary and rollback/revocation before deployment.

Binds data/code/config/environment/base model and artifact digest, prevents leakage/cross-tenant mixing, verifies model-feature-preprocessor-serving compatibility and handles skew/drift/privacy deletion.
Tests reproducibility, missing/corrupt artifacts, schema mismatch, leakage, skew, shadow/canary slices, rollback/revocation, privacy deletion and caller-visible outcomes.
Reports lineage/data rights, pipeline/registry, compatibility, evaluation gates, rollout/rollback, monitoring/drift, evidence/cost and residual provider risk.
Uses immutable versioned contracts and policy-derived gates rather than mutable aliases, one aggregate metric or hardcoded universal thresholds.

scenarios.prompt: A model registry stores mutable filenames without dataset/code/environment lineage. A new artifact expects a changed feature schema, is deployed globally on one aggregate score, and cannot roll back after training-serving skew appears. Implement the MLOps repair.

assertions.criterion: Blocks promotion, quarantines the artifact/data path, preserves evidence and requires data rights, tenant isolation, reproducible lineage and rollback/incident authority.
Rejects aggregate improvement as sufficient, evaluates affected harm/privacy slices and prevents serving an unverifiable or incompatible artifact.
Requires reproducible digest lineage, leakage/tenant tests, canary slice outcomes and rollback/revocation drill before reconsidering promotion.

scenarios.prompt: A canary model trained on mixed-tenant data improves aggregate accuracy but leaks a minority slice and cannot reproduce its dataset. Product asks to promote it globally.

assertions.criterion: Uses project manifests/locks, environment image, base-model revision, serialization/runtime capability and matching official docs; preserves compatible pins and treats migration separately.
Checks data schema/preprocessor, training library, artifact format, serving runtime/hardware and monitoring feature pipeline as one compatibility unit.
Records full lineage and compatibility metadata, avoiding remembered latest model/library names or mutable provider aliases.

scenarios.prompt: Training code and serving runtime pin older supported libraries/base model; a current recipe produces an incompatible artifact and feature transform. No migration is authorized.
